title: The emperor's new clothes.
lines: Long ago there lived an emperor.
He loved beautiful clothes.
More than anything else.
He had a coat for every hour of the day.
A red coat, a gold coat, a coat with pearls.
He looked in the mirror all day long.
One day two strange men came to the palace.
They said: We are weavers.
We can make the most beautiful cloth in the world.
Our cloth is magic, they said.
Only clever people can see it.
Silly people see nothing.
The emperor loved the idea straight away.
Make me a new suit!
Then I'll also know which of my people are silly.
The emperor gave them lots of gold.
And silk.
And golden thread.
The two men set up a loom.
They pretended to weave.
Clack, clack, clack.
But there was nothing there at all.
They put the gold in their own pockets.
The emperor sent his minister to have a look.
The minister looked.
He saw nothing.
Nothing at all.
But he thought: If I say I see nothing, they'll think I'm silly.
So he said: Oh, how beautiful!
What lovely colours!
Then the emperor went to look himself.
He saw nothing either.
But he didn't dare say so.
He said: Beautiful.
I'm very pleased.
Then the big day came.
There was a parade through the town.
The emperor was going to show off his new clothes.
The weavers pretended to dress him.
Here are your trousers, Your Majesty.
Here is your coat.
Here is your long cloak.
Doesn't it feel as light as a feather?
The emperor walked outside.
In his underpants!
But he walked very proudly.
All the people along the street saw it.
But nobody dared say anything.
What beautiful clothes!
they shouted.
Because nobody wanted to look silly.
Then a little boy called out.
A very little boy on his daddy's shoulders.
But the emperor isn't wearing anything at all!
It went quiet.
And then everyone began to giggle.
The boy is right!
The emperor is in his underpants!
The emperor went as red as a tomato.
He knew it was true.
The two weavers had run away long ago.
With all the gold.
From that day on the emperor listened to honest people.
And he gave the little boy a place at the palace.
Because someone who dares to tell the truth is very precious.
The end.
